title: Normal mechanical breath
نفَس آلي طبيعي
objective: Recognise a complete, normal breath on the pressure, flow and volume traces.
التعرف على نفَس آلي طبيعي ومكتمل على منحنيات الضغط والتدفق والحجم.
accessibleDescription: Pressure rises smoothly from the set PEEP of 5 cmH2O to a peak of about 25 cmH2O over one second, then drops back to 5 cmH2O and stays flat for the rest of the breath.
Flow rises immediately to a constant +40 L/min for one second (inspiration), then reverses to about -40 L/min and decays smoothly back to zero before the next breath begins.
Volume rises in a straight line from 0 to 500 mL during inspiration, then falls back to 0 mL during expiration, reaching zero before the next breath starts.

question.prompt: What does this set of waveforms show?
options: A normal breath, with exhalation completing before the next breath starts
Flow starvation from patient effort exceeding the set flow
question.explanation: The expiratory flow trace returns all the way to zero, and volume returns to zero, before the next inspiration begins - exhalation is complete. The pressure trace returns cleanly to the set PEEP and stays flat, with no residual elevation. There is no scooping or asynchrony in the pressure trace during inspiration.

title: Auto-PEEP (incomplete exhalation)
الضغط الإيجابي الذاتي (زفير غير مكتمل)
objective: Identify incomplete exhalation (auto-PEEP / dynamic hyperinflation) on the flow trace.
تحديد الزفير غير المكتمل (الضغط الإيجابي الذاتي) على منحنى التدفق.
accessibleDescription: Pressure falls after inspiration but does not return to the set PEEP of 5 cmH2O - it settles at about 8 cmH2O, higher than set, and stays there until the next breath interrupts it.
Flow reverses to about -45 L/min at the start of expiration and decays, but at the moment the next breath begins, flow is still at about -8 L/min - it never reached zero.
Volume falls during expiration but does not reach 0 mL before the next breath adds more volume on top - about 80 mL is left over, breath after breath.

question.prompt: What does this set of waveforms show?
options: A normal breath, with exhalation completing before the next breath starts
Flow starvation from patient effort exceeding the set flow
question.explanation: The expiratory flow trace never returns to zero before the next breath begins - this is the characteristic sign of incomplete exhalation (auto-PEEP, dynamic hyperinflation). Volume and pressure both carry over into the next breath instead of returning to baseline, consistent with gas being trapped breath after breath.

title: Flow starvation
نقص التدفق
objective: Identify flow starvation (a scooped pressure trace) during a volume-controlled breath.
تحديد نقص التدفق (منحنى ضغط متقعّر) أثناء نفَس محدد الحجم.
accessibleDescription: Pressure rises at the start of inspiration, then dips down to about 8 cmH2O around a third of the way through the breath - a concave, scooped-out shape - before rising again to a peak near the end of inspiration.

Flow is the same fixed square wave as a normal breath: a constant +40 L/min for one second, then a decaying negative flow during expiration. The flow shape itself does not change, because it is set by the ventilator, not the patient.
Volume still rises in a straight line to 500 mL, because volume control guarantees the set volume regardless of the pressure shape.

question.prompt: What does this set of waveforms show?
options: A normal breath, with exhalation completing before the next breath starts
Flow starvation from patient effort exceeding the set flow
question.explanation: The pressure trace dips and forms a concave, "scooped" shape in the first part of inspiration, while the flow trace stays a fixed square wave. This mismatch - the patient visibly straining against a fixed flow that does not speed up to meet their demand - is the classic appearance of flow starvation, not auto-PEEP (expiratory flow still returns fully to zero here) or a normal breath.
